title: First Glare
summary: Kael enters the Last Drop looking for shade. A scarred patron sees an old enemy in his silhouette and throws a bottle before Kael has said who he is.

panelPlan.text: Wide interior: Kael is framed by blinding white daylight in the swinging doors; a scarred patron kicks back from a corner table with a bottle in hand.
The patron hurls the bottle. Kael only shifts one shoulder; amber glass explodes on the doorframe as Eva watches from a back stool with a ledger.
Kael plucks a glass sliver from his coat and starts toward the unlit table at the back while the room decides what his lack of reaction means.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: A full bottle doesn’t ride the draft like that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Is the table by the back wall open?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I was looking right at your boots.

title: The Table in Shadow
summary: The patron tries again at close range. Kael puts him on the floor without turning the room into a gunfight; Eva immediately starts testing what that restraint means.

panelPlan.text: The patron lunges with a wide punch through the aisle.
Kael catches the wrist, turns with the momentum and puts the man face-down on the boards; hands around the room drift toward holsters.
Kael drags a chair into the darkest available corner. Eva closes the ledger and blocks the aisle rather than giving him distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You left him his teeth. He’s going to wake up and talk.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Is the bench by the draft vent taken?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You’re not even going to ask who he thought you were?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: There’s a nail coming through my boot.

title: Fueling the Rig
summary: Outside, Jessa fuels the rig while Eva watches the saloon from the roof. A crash inside turns routine departure work into a countdown.

panelPlan.text: Jessa leans her weight into a manual brass fuel pump beside the battered rig; Eva sits cross-legged on the roof watching the saloon doors.
A muffled crash comes from the saloon. Eva writes one line in the ledger; Jessa checks the leaking nozzle without looking up.
Jessa drops the hose, kicks the wheel chocks clear and moves for the starter while Eva stands on the roof and points toward movement on the porch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Three of them just came out sideways.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Is the needle past the red mark?

title: Dead Weight
summary: Kael uses the saloon back door and finds a man choking at the end of a rope. Cutting him down creates a new mistaken identity before the man has caught his breath.

panelPlan.text: Kael steps into the blinding back-lot light and sees boots thrashing below a loading beam. He opens a folding knife.
Kael catches the hanging man by the belt, tells him to tuck his chin, and saws through the taut hemp.
The man drops coughing into the dirt. Marcus and two armed locals spill through the back doors, stop in the glare, and stare at Kael as if a dead man has just returned.

title: The Wrong Man Again
summary: Marcus charges because Kael’s silhouette completes a story already running in his head. Eva arrives in time to see Kael refuse the role rather than win it.

panelPlan.text: Marcus comes off the porch with a length of pipe raised over one shoulder. Kael is still kneeling beside the gasping man.
Kael steps aside at the last possible moment; the pipe buries itself in a brittle fence post and Marcus has to wrench it free.
Eva appears at the corner of the lot. Kael points her to the cut rope and the man on the ground instead of turning the moment into a duel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You don’t get to walk back in here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You expect me to believe that face?

title: Moving Before It Settles
summary: Jessa brings the rig around while the settlement argues over who Kael is. Kael does one more practical thing for the injured man and leaves before the argument can settle.

panelPlan.text: The rig rolls into the back lot in a cloud of dust, Jessa already reaching across to shove the passenger door open.
Kael braces the cut-down man against the porch post and puts the severed rope into Marcus’s hands. Around them, locals disagree about the name they think they recognize.
Eva climbs onto the side ladder. Kael gets in only when Marcus turns to the injured man rather than the drifter. Jessa drops the clutch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That’s more than you told me.

title: Passing Through
summary: The rig clears the settlement and joins a route already in motion. Eva chooses to keep following because Kael mattered to strangers without ever claiming the role they offered him.

panelPlan.text: Long horizontal: the rig crosses hard white ground while a passing convoy slides across the far route without stopping.
Eva sits on the rear step with her ledger closed for once. Kael watches the convoy rather than the settlement falling behind.
Final quiet panel: Jessa drives. Eva looks at Kael. He does not turn toward her. The convoy passes through the glare.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You didn’t have to go out the back.
